item.title: Quick Start
item.description:
Run it manually

Download the prebuilt binary for your architecture from the releases section of the GitHub repo. Make the binary executable and run it.

Available Binaries

File Name Description
aralez-x86_64-musl.gz Static Linux x86_64 binary, without any system dependency
aralez-x86_64-glibc.gz Dynamic Linux x86_64 binary, with minimal system dependencies
aralez-x86_64-compat-musl.gz Static Linux x86_64 binary, compatible with old pre Haswell CPUs
aralez-x86_64-compat-glibc.gz Dynamic Linux x86_64 binary, compatible with old pre Haswell CPUs
aralez-aarch64-musl.gz Static Linux ARM64 binary, without any system dependency
aralez-aarch64-glibc.gz Dynamic Linux ARM64 binary, with minimal system dependencies
sadoyan/aralez Docker image on Debian 13 slim (https://hub.docker.com/r/sadoyan/aralez)

Steps

  1. Download the latest release for your architecture from Releases:
wget https://github.com/sadoyan/aralez/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/aralez-xxx-yyy.tar.gz
tar -xzf aralez-xxx-yyy.tar.gz
  1. Make it executable:
chmod +x aralez-xxx-yyy
  1. Copy example configuration and adjust to your needs:
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sadoyan/aralez/refs/heads/main/etc/main.yaml
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sadoyan/aralez/refs/heads/main/etc/upstreams.yaml

  1. Edit to match your needs.

item.title: Cache
item.description:
Caching is disabled if the cache: block is commented out or omitted. Aralez supports three storage backends:

  • memory: Content is stored entirely in local RAM.
    • Performance: Blazing fast with the lowest possible latency.
    • Persistence: Ephemeral; data does not survive process restarts.
    • Use Case: Ideal for single-instance setups requiring maximum speed and zero storage configuration overhead.
  • hybrid: Content is tiered between local RAM and the local file system.
    • Capacity: Allows cache sizes significantly larger than available physical RAM.
    • Tier Management: Hot and cold items are dynamically balanced across memory and disk.
    • Persistence: Memory states are periodically flushed to disk. Only flushed data survives restarts; any changes made after the last flush will be lost.
    • Disk Behavior: Expired data is lazily overwritten rather than actively purged, meaning the file system storage will quickly grow to its maximum configured capacity and remain stable at that size.
    • Use Case: Ideal for datasets larger than available RAM that require high-capacity local storage and persistence across restarts without an external Redis cluster.
  • redis: Uses external RESP-compatible servers (e.g., Redis, Valkey, Dragonfly, KeyDB) as a centralized cache storage layer.
    • Architecture: Requires an accessible external RESP-compliant cluster or instance.
    • Persistence: Handled externally by the database layer.
    • Use Case: Essential for horizontal scaling where multiple Aralez proxy instances need to share a unified cache pool.
  • tikv Uses a distributed transactional and raw key-value store (TiKV) backed by Placement Driver (PD) endpoints as a centralized, highly scalable cache storage layer.
    • Architecture: Requires an accessible external TiKV cluster with list of or single PD endpoints (e.g., tikv://127.0.0.1:2379,127.0.0.2:2379).
    • Capacity: Horizontally scalable and distributed, allowing massive cache capacities far beyond single-node RAM or disk and Redis limits.
    • Persistence: Handled externally and reliably by the distributed TiKV cluster storage engine.
    • Requires: Externally running TiKV cluster with enabled TTL.
      • TTL must be enabled on TiKV cluster otherwise cache will fail to write data. How to enable ttl on TiKV:
    • Use Case: Ideal for distributed, high-availability deployments where multiple Aralez proxy instances require a fault-tolerant, and horizontally scalable unified cache pool.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
main.yaml — Startup Parameters

Key Example Value Description
threads 12 Number of worker threads assigned to proxy operations. Defaults to 1.
runuser aralez Optional. Username to run as after dropping root privileges (requires launch as root).
rungroup aralez Optional. Group to run as after dropping root privileges (requires launch as root).
cache Optional Block If omitted entirely, caching is disabled.
cache.storage hybrid Storage backend: "memory", "hybrid", "redis://host:port", or "tikv://host1:port,host2.port". Defaults to "memory".
cache.mem_size_mb 64 Optional. Memory cache tier limit in megabytes. Defaults to 64.
cache.file_size_mb 128 Optional. Disk cache tier limit in megabytes (hybrid mode). Defaults to 512.
cache.file_path /tmp/cache Optional. Directory path for the disk cache tier. Defaults to /tmp/aralez_cache.
cache.item_max_size 5 Optional. Maximum allowed size for a single cached item in megabytes. Defaults to 5.
cache.flush_interval 60 Optional. Interval in seconds to flush memory cache states to disk (hybrid mode). Defaults to 60.
cache.ttl 300 Optional. Default TTL in seconds used when upstream Cache-Control headers are absent. Defaults to 300.
upstream_keepalive_pool_size 500 Maximum number of keepalive connections pooled for upstream targets.
pid_file /tmp/aralez.pid File system path where the daemon process ID is written.
error_log /tmp/aralez_err.log Optional. File path for directing standard error log output when enabled.
upgrade_sock /tmp/aralez.sock Unix domain socket path used for zero-downtime binary upgrades and state handoffs.
config_api_enabled true Boolean toggle to enable/disable remote runtime configuration push capability.
config_address 0.0.0.0:3000 HTTP API bind address for pushing runtime config updates.
proxy_address_http 0.0.0.0:6193 Primary bind address and port for incoming plain-text HTTP proxy traffic.
proxy_address_tls 0.0.0.0:6194 Optional bind address and port for incoming secure TLS proxy traffic.
proxy_configs /etc/aralez Path to directory containing SSL certs and keys in format {NAME}.crt and {NAME}.key.
upstreams_conf /etc/aralez/upstreams.yaml File system path pointing to upstream service routing definitions.
proxy_tls_grade high Security grade of TLS cipher suite (high, medium, unsafe). high matches Qualys SSL Labs A+.
file_server_folder /opt/public Optional. Local file system directory to serve statically.
file_server_address 0.0.0.0:3002 Optional. Local bind address for static file server.
log_level info Global logging verbosity threshold (info, warn, error, debug, trace, off).
access_log all Access logging mode (all, error). Omit/comment out to disable.
log_pattern {d(%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S)} {h({l})} - {t} - {m} {n} Optional custom log pattern. Defaults to {d(%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S)} {l} - {m}{n}.
log_file /tmp/aralez.log, 20, 5, compress Optional file logging config: path, max size (MB), rotated files to keep, compression.
log_structured elasticsearch Optional structured logging sink target (e.g., elasticsearch).
acme_dns_provider cloudflare DNS provider API integration for automated ACME DNS-01 challenges (cloudflare, route53, digitalocean).
hc_method HEAD HTTP health check method verb (HEAD, GET, POST in UPPERCASE).
hc_interval 5 Time interval in seconds between periodic upstream health checks.
cluster_member master Optional. Operational role in multi-node cluster mode (master, worker).
worker_nodes http://127.0.0.1:8000, http://127.0.0.1:4000 Required if cluster_member: master. Comma-separated worker management endpoints.
tcp Optional Block Optional advanced Linux TCP socket parameters. Do not alter unless tuned for specific network environments. Values shown act as operational defaults.
tcp.tcp_keepalive_idle 30 Seconds of socket inactivity before sending TCP keepalive probes. Defaults to 30.
tcp.tcp_keepalive_interval 10 Seconds between individual keepalive probes if no response. Defaults to 10.
tcp.tcp_keepalive_count 5 Maximum unanswered probes before declaring connection dead. Defaults to 5.
tcp.so_reuseport true Enables SO_REUSEPORT for multi-worker connection distribution without lock contention. Defaults to true.
tcp.tcp_fastopen 4096 Enables TCP Fast Open backlog queue size. Set to 0 if unsupported by host kernel/container. Defaults to 4096.

Cluster Mode

  • master Master node don’t serve the live traffic. It runs the health checks and updates worker nodes.
  • worker Worker nodes handles the traffic, but the health checks are completely tuened off. Worker nodes wil receive full status from master.
  • Environment variable MASTER_KEY with the same value is required for both master and worker nodes.

Cluster mode is designed for high loaded career proxy farms where hundreds, or thousands of upstreams are configures and there is need to offload heavy health checks and type detections. Currently, a single master is supported, Master consensus with full RAFT implementation is planned.

item.title: API
item.description:
Remote Configuration API

Aralez provides an HTTP API for updating the upstream configuration by pushing a new upstreams.yaml file to config_address, which defaults to 127.0.0.1:3000. This API is useful for automating configuration updates in CI/CD pipelines or managing upstreams remotely.

Authentication

The configuration API requires authentication using the MASTERKEY environment variable. Before enabling the API, make sure the MASTERKEY environment variable is set in the Aralez process environment.`

Each request must provide the master key using one of the following methods:

item.title: Authentication
item.description:
Authentication (Optional)

Authentication works on two levels: Global and per path.

If Global authentication is enabled, per-path authentication is ignored. Both web.example.com and www.example.com in the example below require root:toor credentials from the global section — the per-path admin:admin on www.example.com is overridden.

The same applies to all methods (basic, jwt, api). Global always overrides per-path.

provider: "file"
sticky_sessions: false
to_https: false
rate_limit: 100
authorization:
  type: "basic"
  data: "root:toor"
upstreams:
  web.example.com:
    paths:
      "/":
        servers:
          - "127.0.0.3:8000"
          - "127.0.0.4:8000"
  www.example.com:
    paths:
      "/":
        to_https: false
        authorization:
          type: "basic"
          data: "admin:admin"
        servers:
          - "127.0.0.1:8000"
          - "127.0.0.2:8000"

item.title: Benchmarks
item.description:
Methodology and Profile

Benchmarks are performed by Oha HTTP benchmark tool.

Proxies tested: Aralez Glibc, Aralez Musl, HAProxy, Envoy, NginX, Traefik, Caddy

Load profile:

  • Proxy servers running on same host with different ports
  • 4× Oha instances for parallel testing of GET/POST requests
  • 3× Upstream servers on separate machines with sample JSON file responses
  • Tuned Kernel parameters for heavy load
  • 10 Gbit network
  • All instances: 4 Core+HT Intel Xeon CPU E5-2699C v4 @ 2.20GHz
  • 60 URLs (deep / nested paths), majority HTTPS (TLS termination active)
  • Mixed GET + POST, JSON payload for POST
  • 4 × 1024 / 2048 / 4096 / 8192 / 16384 / 32768 concurrent connections
  • Upstreams on separate machines, no caching

Benchmark Results

Results shown are from 1 of 4 concurrent Oha instances. Success Rate includes all responses (2xx, 4xx, 5xx); real success rates are lower for all servers.

item.title: Prometheus Metrics
item.description:
Prometheus metrics are exposed at http://config_address/metrics — by default http://127.0.0.1:3000/metrics.

Example Grafana Dashboard

Metric Summary Table

Metric Name Type Unit Description
aralez_active_sessions Gauge Count Current number of active user/client sessions.
aralez_cache_evicted_bytes_total Gauge Bytes Total memory size of data evicted from the cache.
aralez_cache_evicted_items_total Gauge Count Total number of individual items evicted from the cache.
aralez_cache_items Gauge Count Current total number of items stored in the cache.
aralez_cache_size_bytes Gauge Bytes Current memory consumption of the cache in bytes.
aralez_cache_status Counter Counter Phases of cached responses
aralez_logging_errors Gauge / Counter Count Total count of logging error events recorded.
aralez_memory_bytes Gauge Bytes Total memory currently allocated by the process in bytes.
aralez_open_files Gauge Count Number of open file descriptors currently held by the application.
aralez_requests_by_method_total Counter Count Total HTTP requests processed, partitioned by HTTP method.
aralez_requests_by_upstream Counter Count Total HTTP requests routed, partitioned by targeted upstream server.
aralez_requests_by_version_total Counter Count Total HTTP requests received, partitioned by HTTP protocol version.
aralez_requests_total Counter Count Aggregate count of all HTTP requests handled by Aralez.
aralez_response_latency_seconds Histogram Seconds Distribution of HTTP response latency in seconds.
aralez_responses_total Counter Count Total HTTP responses returned, partitioned by HTTP status code.

Detailed Metric Breakdown

1. Request & Response Metrics

aralez_requests_total

  • Type: Counter
  • Description: Tracks the cumulative number of HTTP requests processed by the Aralez application since process start.
  • Usage: Calculate overall throughput using PromQL: rate(aralez_requests_total[5m]).

aralez_requests_by_method_total

  • Type: Counter
  • Labels:
    • method: The HTTP request method (e.g., GET, POST, PUT, HEAD).
  • Description: Tracks request traffic broken down by HTTP protocol verb.

aralez_requests_by_version_total

  • Type: Counter
  • Labels:
    • version: The HTTP protocol version used (e.g., HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2.0).
  • Description: Breakdown of request volume by protocol version.

aralez_requests_by_upstream

  • Type: Counter
  • Labels:
    • upstream: Hostname or IP of the destination upstream server (e.g., localhost, apt.netangels.net).
  • Description: Tracks traffic distribution across upstream backend dependencies.

aralez_responses_total

  • Type: Counter
  • Labels:
    • status: HTTP response status code (e.g., 200, 502).
  • Description: Total responses generated, grouped by HTTP response code.
  • Usage: Useful for calculating error rates (e.g., ratio of 5xx responses to total responses).

aralez_response_latency_seconds

  • Type: Histogram
  • Associated Metrics:
    • aralez_response_latency_seconds_bucket{le="..."}: Count of requests completed within the specified latency threshold (le = less than or equal to seconds).
    • aralez_response_latency_seconds_sum: Cumulative total of all response latencies in seconds.
    • aralez_response_latency_seconds_count: Total number of measured requests (matches aralez_requests_total).
  • Description: Measures request execution duration to calculate percentiles (p50, p95, p99).
  • Usage: Calculate 95th percentile latency over 5 minutes: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(aralez_response_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

2. Cache Metrics

aralez_cache_items

  • Type: Gauge
  • Description: Instantaneous measurement of the number of items currently held in memory cache.

aralez_cache_size_bytes

  • Type: Gauge
  • Description: Current memory consumption of the active cache in bytes.

aralez_cache_evicted_items_total

  • Type: Gauge (Behaves as Counter)
  • Description: Cumulative number of objects removed from the cache due to memory limits or eviction policies.

aralez_cache_evicted_bytes_total

  • Type: Gauge (Behaves as Counter)
  • Description: Cumulative size (in bytes) of all objects evicted from the cache.

3. System & Session Metrics

aralez_active_sessions

  • Type: Gauge
  • Description: Real-time count of currently connected or active client sessions.

aralez_memory_bytes

  • Type: Gauge
  • Description: Current memory allocated by the application process (in bytes).

aralez_open_files

  • Type: Gauge
  • Description: Number of open file handles currently used by the process. Monitor to prevent hitting operating system file descriptor limits (ulimit).

aralez_logging_errors

  • Type: Gauge
  • Description: Count of error events logged by the application system.

item.title: Kubernetes Ingress
item.description:
Sett up Aralez inside as a Kubernetes ingress controller.

Create the necessary ServiceAccount, apply the right RBAC roles, and deploy Aralez as a Kubernetes Deployment with an exposed Service.

Step 1: Create a Service Account

Aralez needs a ServiceAccount with permissions to watch Kubernetes resources like pods, endpoints, and services.

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: aralez-sa

Step 2: Define RBAC Permissions

Aralez requires read-only access to Kubernetes resources within a namespace.

item.title: Manage Certificates
item.description:
TLS basics

TLS (HTTPS) is off until you turn it on. To enable it:

  1. Set proxy_address_tls in main.yaml.
  2. Put at least one certificate and key pair (NAME.crt and NAME.key) in the certificates directory.
  3. New certificates and key will be loaded on the fly without rest.

Aralez needs a first certificate and key pair to start the TLS listener. This pair can be anything, including a self-signed certificate for a dummy domain. Once you have a real certificate, you can delete it.

item.title: Consul Integration
item.description:
Make sure you have access to Consul API. Add Consul servers in upstreams file. If consul authentication is enabled , get API token and add to config file. All configs except authentication at virtual host / path level are working as with configuration via plain config file .

Aralez can be deployed, both as Nomad services or as a stand-alone application. The only requirement is access to API of consul servers, and Nomad services ServicePort & ServiceAddress
